generators.label: Mixed primary uses
generators.summary: People on the street at different times, for different purposes.

generators.label: Short blocks
generators.summary: Frequent streets and chances to turn corners.

generators.label: Aged buildings
generators.summary: A mingling of buildings of different ages and rents.
generators.status: needs BAG construction years (see issue tracker)

generators.label: Concentration
generators.summary: A dense enough concentration of people, residents included.

metrics.label: Use mix
metrics.description: Evenness of open places across six kinds of use (work, shopping, food & drink, personal services, civic, culture & leisure). Shannon entropy scaled to 0–1; hexagons with fewer than 5 places are left blank.

metrics.label: Places per ha
metrics.description: Open shops, offices, cafés, schools, clinics and other places per hectare of land.

metrics.label: Places per 100 addresses
metrics.description: Non-residential activity relative to the number of addresses: low values mean mostly homes, very high values mostly business.

metrics.label: Street intersections
metrics.description: Street intersections (three or more ways) per km² of land. Footpaths through green space are not counted.

metrics.label: Street length between corners
metrics.description: Median length of street between two intersections: Jacobs' block length.

metrics.label: Block size
metrics.description: Median area of the blocks enclosed by streets (blocks over 25 ha are left out).

metrics.label: Path intersections
metrics.description: Intersections on the full walking network, footpaths included. Compare with street intersections to see where permeability comes from paths in green space.

metrics.label: Addresses per ha
metrics.description: BAG addresses (homes and other units) per hectare of land, gross. Jacobs' threshold of about 100 dwellings per net acre is roughly 250 per net hectare.

metrics.label: Building coverage
metrics.description: Share of land covered by building footprints (GSI).

areas.label: Oude Noorden
areas.note: 19th-century working-class district, fine grain, mixed ground floors.

areas.label: Oude Westen
areas.note: 19th-century district that residents saved from planned clearance in the 1970s.

areas.label: Lijnbaan / Cool
areas.note: Rebuilt after 1940; the Lijnbaan (1953) was Europe's first purpose-built pedestrian shopping street.

areas.label: Ommoord
areas.note: 1960s-70s modernist expansion with high-rise slabs in green space.

areas.label: Kop van Zuid
areas.note: 1990s-2010s redevelopment of former docks into a high-rise district.

areas.label: Pendrecht
areas.note: 1950s "neighbourhood unit" garden district, repeated stamps of housing around greens.
